CHALLENGE 11 / COORDINATES · DISTANCE · LOGICAL THINKING · SEEDED GENERATION

FIELD GUIDE / 20–30 MINUTES

Follow the clues.
Trust your thinking.

  1. Pick a square. The island has columns A–E and rows 1–5. Find its one hidden treasure within six unique digs.
  2. Read the distance. A clue of 3 means three horizontal + vertical steps. No diagonal shortcuts. For example, A1 to C2 is 2 across + 1 down = 3.
  3. Use your compass. After two misses, it points from your latest dig towards the treasure. A diagonal compass hint means move in both named directions, one grid step at a time.
  4. Make a prediction. Combine all your clues before digging again. The optional reasoning lens checks which squares fit the evidence.
  5. Replay the experiment. Restart keeps the active seed and treasure. The same first dig gives the same clue. New island creates a different seed.
Try it as a class

Take turns as navigator, clue recorder, and sceptic. Before each dig, explain which clue supports your choice. Then restart and test whether you can reproduce the same results.

Seed science: a seed is text that starts a predictable number generator. It gives the same treasure every time. Different seeds can sometimes hide treasure in the same square: there are only 25 squares!

This file works locally with no libraries, accounts, external requests or paid services. Narration is bundled Sonia audio.
